story.head: Strength vs. Strength
paras: The Bruins won the teams’ first meeting this season, 4-1 in Los Angeles on Oct 17. The Bruins (13-5-1) lost 5-2 to Montréal on Thursday, and the Kings are on a three-game losing streak. Going in, the Kings are seventh in the Pacific (30th in the NHL) and the Bruins third in the Atlantic (tied for eighth).

The Kings have played better than their record (.353) says: their chances are worth about .629, and their finishing has held them back. The Bruins’ record (.711) is running ahead of what their chances are worth (.562), largely thanks to their goaltending.

The Bruins (lowest) and the Kings (2nd lowest) both leave the shooting to their forwards. The Kings have had shaky goaltending (30th). They also keep dangerous shots away better than almost anyone (2nd), so the Bruins’ good looks will be harder to come by against them. On the other side, the Bruins have had some of the league’s best goaltending (2nd). They also sit back rather than chase on the forecheck (2nd lowest), so the Kings hound the puck, but them sit back. Boston has allowed 2.42 goals a game, the third fewest in the league.

Artemi Panarin (8 G / 11 A / 19 P in 17 GP) leads the Kings in scoring. The Bruins’ scoring runs through David Pastrňák (8 G / 16 A / 24 P in 19 GP), and Elias Lindholm (7 G / 10 A / 17 P in 19 GP) isn’t far behind.
Darcy Kuemper (5-5-1 / .873 SV% in 11 GS) is in line to start for Los Angeles. Jeremy Swayman (9-4-1 / .913 SV% in 14 GS) has been a rock in net for Boston and will likely start.
At home, Marco Sturm likes to send Mittelstadt, Lindholm and Khusnutdinov out against the other team’s top line, so watch for them against Panarin, Laferriere and Kempe.
